## Design

### 2026-10-09 – This is basically my first time making something in KiCad for the purposes of actually putting it into a PCB. I've done some tutorials and used it to make general schematics, but nothing to the precis

**2.12h**

This is basically my first time making something in KiCad for the purposes of actually putting it into a PCB. I've done some tutorials and used it to make general schematics, but nothing to the precision of a thing that should be assembled.

Although I was thinking of using the AtTiny85, I don't think it has enough IO for my purpose. I switched to the more powerful CH32V003, that should have plenty for my needs. I also learned more about Charlieplexing to power all the LEDs.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 135944](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Xt10ZK7FTi1vKiU37U67a1QQj2rKZWIn/69e97716b0d67c6fb8b54c0aa3799848ac9a07e0c826da0731f0d5d31af7c1b8.png)

What I need to get down now is the proper placement on the PCB footprint, get accurate silkscreens.

I think I will also leave space to incorporate usb-c power, so I'll need a good way to switch between power from usb, from a cell battery, or to be off.
